newsitem.title: USA: Five bombs found in raid on New York apartment.
newsitem.headline: Five bombs found in raid on New York apartment.

text.p: Police on Thursday seized five potentially deadly bombs and arrested three men of Middle Eastern origin in a dawn raid on a New York apartment, officials said.
The FBI said "a massive investigation" was under way to find out exactly what the bombs were intended for, whether the suspects were acting as individuals or as a group and the possible motive.
Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said there was no connection between the discovery of the bombs in a residential neighbourhood of Brooklyn and the double suicide bombing of a Jerusalem market on Wednesday.

But he said that one of the men arrested "was yesterday heard expressing support for what happened in Israel." Moslem militants claimed responsibility for killing 13 people and wounding 170 others in Wednesday's attack.
"The individuals involved are Middle Eastern but we don't have definite confirmation of their nations of origin yet," the mayor said.
He said the Joint Terrorism Task Force of local, state and federal agencies was investigating whether there was a possible plot to bomb New York subways or other targets.
"The devices were tested and a determination has been made that they are bombs," Giuliani said. "There are altogether five devices."
New York Police Commissioner Howard Safir said the bombs could have killed or wounded people and damaged buildings if they had been detonated.

"Based on a computer analysis that we did of the amount of explosives and the kind of device, they would kill someone up to 25 feet (7.6 metres) in a confined area and injure someone up to 100 feet (30.5 metres) in an outside area," Safir said.
By Thursday evening, officials were reluctant to comment on any aspects of an investigation said by FBI Assistant Director James Kallstrom to be global.

"As every hour goes by we know more about this ... but we're not going to talk about it," Kallstrom told reporters. "Rest assured that we do have a massive investigation to answer questions: who are these people? what are they doing here? what were their intentions?"
Kallstorm urged the media and the public "not to jump to conclusions" about the suspects.
Police ordered the raid after receiving a tip at 10:45 p.m. EDT on Wednesday (0245 GMT Thursday) that there were explosives or explosive devices in an apartment in the Park Slope neighbourhood.
Officers evacuated 90 residents, closed off a four-block area and diverted subway services during the 4:40 a.m. EDT Thursday (0840 GMT) raid and its aftermath.

They found three men sleeping inside the apartment and the suspicious devices. Officials said the operation took a dramatic turn when two suspects lunged for one of the possible explosive devices and police officers opened fire, wounding them.
Their lives were not in danger and they were in custody in the hospital. Giuliani said that authorities hoped to charge the suspects on Thursday night or on Friday.
The raid created chaos for residents in the neighbourhood as police awoke them in the early hours. About 90 people were evacuated from their homes.

"They were just rushing us out and nobody knew what was going on and then some cops said there was a bomb scare," Edwin Caraballo said. His sister, Evita Caraballo, said, "They were yelling and yelling 'you have to leave, leave the house now because there's a bomb.'"
